quotes/pius-xii-assumed/text: …was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.
quotes/justin-socrates-christians/text: We have been taught that Christ is the first-born of God, and we have declared above that He is the Word of whom every race of men were partakers; and those who lived reasonably are Christians, even though they have been thought atheists; as, among the Greeks, Socrates and Heraclitus, and men like them ...
quotes/cyprian-no-salvation-para/text: Cyprian argued that baptism and salvation belong only to the one Church, since there is no salvation outside the Church (salus extra ecclesiam non est), so that even martyrdom outside her unity cannot save.
quotes/gregory-by-degrees/text: ... for there is no doubt that it is impossible to efface every thing at once from their obdurate minds; because he who endeavours to ascend to the highest place, rises by degrees or steps, and not by leaps.
quotes/ricci-confucian-para/text: Ricci argued that the ancient Chinese classics already knew the Lord on High (Shangdi), whom Christians call the Lord of Heaven, and that later Neo-Confucian materialism, not Confucius, had obscured this truth.
quotes/carey-enquiry-para/text: Carey contended that the command to teach all nations was not confined to the apostles but binds Christians in every age, and that believers are obliged to use every lawful means, forming societies, sending missionaries and giving money, for the conversion of the heathen.
quotes/venn-euthanasia-para/text: Venn taught that the aim of a mission is a native church that is self-supporting, self-governing and self-extending; once that is reached the missionary should move on, which he called "the euthanasia of a mission".
quotes/kraemer-discontinuity-para/text: Kraemer held that the revelation in Christ stands in radical discontinuity with every religion, including empirical Christianity; religions are human achievements, noble and sinful, judged and yet sought by God’s self-disclosure.
quotes/rahner-anonymous-para/text: Rahner argued that because God wills all to be saved, grace must be offered to every person, and that non-Christians who accept it in conscience, even through their own religions, may be called "anonymous Christians" saved by Christ though they do not know him by name.
quotes/nostra-aetate-true-holy-para/text: The Council taught that the Catholic Church rejects nothing that is true and holy in other religions, regarding with sincere respect their ways of life and teachings, which often reflect a ray of the Truth that enlightens all people, while it proclaims Christ as the way, the truth and the life.
quotes/dignitatis-humanae-para/text: Dignitatis Humanae declares that the human person has a right to religious freedom, meaning immunity from coercion by individuals, groups or any human power, so that no one is forced to act against conscience in religious matters, a right grounded in the dignity of the person known through revelation and reason.
quotes/hick-copernican-para/text: Hick called for a Copernican revolution in theology: instead of placing Christianity at the centre with other religions revolving around it, Christians should recognise that God (the Real) is at the centre and that all the great faiths revolve around and respond to that one divine reality.
quotes/dominus-iesus-para/text: Dominus Iesus insists that Jesus Christ is the unique and universal mediator of salvation and that the Church is necessary for salvation; it rejects theories that treat religions as equal paths, while affirming that non-Christians can receive grace, though objectively in a gravely deficient situation compared with those in the Church.
quotes/pinnock-wideness-para/text: Pinnock argued that God’s boundless generosity means everyone has access to saving grace; people like Job, Melchizedek and the "holy pagans" of Scripture show that those who respond in faith to the light they have can be saved by Christ, even without hearing of him.
quotes/sanneh-translation-para/text: Sanneh argued that by translating the Bible into local languages, missions made the vernacular a vehicle of revelation, thereby relativising Western culture and stimulating indigenous renewal and resistance that often outran missionary and colonial control.
quotes/padilla-integral-para/text: Padilla argued that evangelism and social responsibility are inseparable dimensions of the gospel of the kingdom, and that much missionary preaching was captive to a Western consumerist culture that offered cheap grace without discipleship.
quotes/schleiermacher-absolute-dependenc: The self-identical essence of piety is this: the consciousness of being absolutely dependent, or, which is the same thing, of being in relation with God.
quotes/campbell-where-scriptures-speak/t: Where the Scriptures speak, we speak; and where the Scriptures are silent, we are silent.
quotes/joseph-smith-bible-and-book-of-mo: We believe the Bible to be the word of God as far as it is translated correctly; we also believe the Book of Mormon to be the word of God.
quotes/russell-divine-plan-para/text: Russell taught that the Bible reveals a "divine plan of the ages" with a precise chronology, that Christ’s return would be an invisible presence, and that the "Gentile Times" would end in 1914; he rejected the Trinity, the immortality of the soul and eternal torment.
quotes/harnack-father-only/text: The Gospel, as Jesus proclaimed it, has to do with the Father only and not with the Son.
quotes/mott-watchword/text: The Evangelization of the World in This Generation
quotes/fosdick-shall-fundamentalists-par: Fosdick asked whether the churches would make room for Christians who, in the light of modern knowledge, did not hold to inerrancy, a biological virgin birth or a literal second coming, and pleaded for tolerance and liberty within the church rather than exclusion.
quotes/machen-totally-diverse-religion/t: The great redemptive religion which has always been known as Christianity is battling against a totally diverse type of religious belief, which is only the more destructive of the Christian faith because it makes use of traditional Christian terminology.
quotes/barth-romans-para/text: Barth argued that God is "wholly other", that there is an infinite qualitative distinction (in Kierkegaard’s phrase) between God and humanity, and that God’s Word in Christ comes as judgement and grace upon all human religion, including the confident culture-Protestantism of his teachers.
quotes/nee-local-church-para/text: Nee taught that Scripture recognises one church in each locality, governed by local elders and not by foreign missions or denominations, so that Chinese churches should be self-governing, self-supporting and self-propagating under Christ.
quotes/unitatis-redintegratio-para/text: The Council declared that restoring unity among all Christians is one of its principal concerns, since division openly contradicts the will of Christ, scandalises the world and damages the preaching of the gospel; Christians of other communions, justified by faith in baptism, are recognised as brothers and sisters in the Lord.
quotes/lausanne-evangelism-social/text: The Lausanne Covenant affirmed that evangelism and socio-political involvement are both part of Christian duty, expressing penitence that evangelicals had sometimes regarded them as mutually exclusive, while insisting that reconciliation with people is not reconciliation with God.
quotes/walls-southward-shift/text: Walls argued that Christianity is infinitely translatable and has repeatedly moved its centre of gravity, from Jerusalem to the Hellenistic world, to northern Europe, and now to Africa, Asia and Latin America, so that the typical Christian today is no longer Western.
quotes/bell-love-wins-para/text: Bell questioned whether a loving God would consign billions to eternal torment, suggesting that God’s love may ultimately reconcile all things, and that this hope has been held within the Christian tradition before.
quotes/evans-searching-for-sunday-para/t: Evans described leaving the evangelical church of her youth over questions of science, gender and the exclusion of LGBTQ people, and then finding faith renewed through the sacraments and liturgy of a mainline church, not as a return to certainty but to a community of grace.
quotes/justin-spermatic-word/text: For each man spoke well in proportion to the share he had of the spermatic word, seeing what was related to it.
quotes/tertullian-athens-jerusalem/text: What indeed has Athens to do with Jerusalem? What concord is there between the Academy and the Church? what between heretics and Christians?
quotes/john-damascus-ishmaelites/text: John of Damascus describes Islam as the latest of the heresies, “forerunner of the Antichrist”, says that Muhammad, having encountered the Old and New Testaments and an Arian monk, devised his own heresy, and challenges the lack of witnesses to his prophetic call.
quotes/timothy-mahdi-para/text: Asked by the caliph what he thought of Muhammad, Timothy answers that Muhammad walked in the path of the prophets, since he taught the unity of God, opposed idolatry and fought for God — while courteously declining to call him a prophet and defending the Trinity by analogies such as the sun with its light and heat.
quotes/abu-qurrah-true-religion/text: Abu Qurrah imagines a man raised in isolation who meets representatives of many religions; reason, he argues, can judge which religion’s account of God, sin and salvation best fits what human nature shows us — and that test favours Christianity.
quotes/anselm-believe-to-understand/text: For I do not seek to understand that I may believe, but I believe in order to understand.
quotes/aquinas-five-ways/text: The existence of God can be proved in five ways.
quotes/aquinas-preambles-para/text: Aquinas distinguishes truths about God that reason can reach — such as that God exists and is one — from those that exceed reason, such as the Trinity; even the former are fittingly revealed, since otherwise few would know them, after long time, and mixed with error.
quotes/calvin-sense-of-deity/text: That there exists in the human mind, and indeed by natural instinct, some sense of Deity, we hold to be beyond dispute.
quotes/pascal-wager-para/text: Pascal argues that reason cannot settle whether God exists, yet we must wager, since not to choose is to choose; if you bet on God and win, you gain everything, and if you lose, you lose nothing of value — so wager without hesitation, and act as believers do until belief comes.
quotes/pascal-heart-reasons-para/text: Pascal says that the heart has its reasons which reason does not know: we know God and first principles by the heart, not by reason alone.
quotes/butler-probability-guide/text: But to us, probability is the very guide of life.
quotes/hume-design-para/text: Through his character Philo, Hume argues that the analogy between the universe and a human artefact is weak; even granted, it would prove at most a limited, perhaps fallible or multiple designer, not the infinite and perfectly good God of theism, especially given the evils of the world.
quotes/paley-heath/text: In crossing a heath, suppose I pitched my foot against a stone, and were asked how the stone came to be there; I might possibly answer, that, for any thing I knew to the contrary, it had lain there for ever.
